clue.text: Troops confronting friendly power — surely not?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a regiment of the British Army
a nation on your side in a war is an ally

explanation.surface: Soldiers facing a supposedly friendly nation and reacting with disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: Both express incredulity: an exclamation of doubt said to someone making an unlikely claim.

clue.text: Newton saw through this philosopher's statement

definitions.text: Newton saw through this philosopher's statement

parts.words: Newton saw through this philosopher's statement
parts.note: Newton built a telescope using a mirror, and a philosopher is one who thinks deeply or ponders

explanation.surface: Newton exposed the falsity of a thinker's claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw through' suggests seeing past a lie, but Newton literally looked through his mirror telescope; a philosopher is also one who ponders.
explanation.definitionFit: Newton invented the mirror-based telescope, and a thinker who ponders things is one who reflects.

clue.text: Where Corydon and Daphnis, for starters, may have burst into song?

definitions.text: Where Corydon and Daphnis, for starters, may have burst into song?

indicators.note: burst into means the starting letters break inside the other word

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera

indicators.note: for starters means take the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: Wondering where two classical shepherds might have begun singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst into' looks like the singing itself, but signals a container. Corydon and Daphnis are shepherd-singers of classical pastoral poetry, set in an idyllic region of Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is the idealised rural land of pastoral verse, home of shepherd-singers like these two.

clue.text: Part of body I have held in two hands

indicators.note: held in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, the two hands
I have shortens to I've

explanation.surface: Something the speaker holds between both hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver is an organ, a part of the human body.

clue.text: Menacing misdeed I almost back

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing or misdeed

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter here

parts.note: the stern is the back part of a ship

explanation.surface: A threatening wrong that the speaker nearly supports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims STERN to STER; 'back' looks like a verb (support) but is the rear of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sinister is threatening or suggestive of harm, the same as menacing.

clue.text: Such a parade isn't supposed be entirely innocent

definitions.text: Such a parade isn't supposed be entirely innocent

parts.words: Such a parade isn't supposed be entirely innocent
parts.note: a police line-up of people, one of whom is the suspect, so not all are blameless

explanation.surface: A procession that is not meant to be wholly blameless.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is printed missing 'to' after 'supposed'; read it as 'isn't supposed to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: In an identity parade one member is the suspect, so its line-up is not meant to be all innocent people.

clue.text: Bury Matilda, perhaps, right away, among other things

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: right away means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: Matilda in Hilaire Belloc's cautionary poem told such dreadful lies, so she is a liar

explanation.surface: Burying someone called Matilda at once, along with other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but removes R from A LIAR. Belloc's Matilda told lies and was burned to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is Latin for among other things.

clue.text: During rounds, a doctor's seen construction of sewers

indicators.note: during means the other pieces come within this word

parts.note: a tour is a round of visits
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor seen on rounds while drains are being built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewers' looks like drains but means people who sew.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambour is a circular frame used in embroidery, something built for needleworkers.

clue.text: Annoyed with idler's dissipation

indicators.note: dissipation means the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Irritated by a lazy person's dissolute living.
explanation.definitionFit: To be riled is to be irritated, the same as annoyed.

clue.text: Be unable to decide to fit waste to typical water supply

parts.note: to blow money is to waste it
a usual home has both hot and cold taps

explanation.surface: Dithering over whether to connect a waste pipe to the mains.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow hot and cold is an idiom for vacillating, unable to commit.

clue.text: For Helen, a thousand ships not an excessive price

definitions.meaning: Helen of Troy had the face that launched a thousand ships, so that was what her looks were worth
paying the printed price on a ticket or share, no more than its nominal worth

explanation.surface: Helen of Troy's beauty was worth a fleet, which is not overpriced.
explanation.definitionFit: The nominal or printed price of something, and what a face is worth: Marlowe's line on Helen's face launching a thousand ships.

clue.text: Indian male kept in shadow

indicators.note: kept in means one piece is held inside another word

parts.note: to tail someone is to shadow or follow them; as a noun a tail is a shadower

explanation.surface: An Indian man held in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamils are a people of southern India and Sri Lanka, so a Tamil is an Indian.

clue.text: Two European varieties of the shrub

parts.note: the definite article in Spanish is el and in German der: two European versions of the word the
the definite article in Spanish is el and in German der: two European versions of the word the

explanation.surface: Two kinds of a bush found in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' looks like part of 'of the shrub', but it is the word being translated: Spanish EL and German DER.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a common shrub or small tree bearing white flowers and dark berries.

clue.text: West of crossing point, river perhaps appears as crystal

indicators.note: in an across answer, west of means coming before, to the left

parts.note: a river is an example of water
a ford is a shallow place where a river can be crossed

explanation.surface: Describing a river near a ford looking clear as crystal.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterford is a famous brand of cut glass from Ireland, so crystal is the class it belongs to.

clue.text: Leaves a little extra that's gone to pot?

definitions.text: Leaves a little extra that's gone to pot?

parts.words: Leaves a little extra that's gone to pot?
parts.note: tea leaves measured with a small spoon, traditionally adding one extra measure for the pot when brewing

explanation.surface: Leftovers wasted and ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone to pot' means ruined, but here it is literal: the extra spoon of tea leaves goes in the teapot.
explanation.definitionFit: The old rule for brewing tea is one spoonful per person and one for the pot.

clue.text: Nancy appearing in feeble play about 2?

indicators.note: appearing in means one piece shows up inside the other

parts.note: pale can mean weak or feeble
Nancy Astor was the first woman to sit in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A woman named Nancy acting in a weak play.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 refers to the answer to 2 Down, an idyllic rural land.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastorale is a musical or dramatic work on a rural theme, set in such a land.

clue.text: Criticise talking over music

definitions.meaning: rhythmic speech delivered over a beat, as in hip-hop

explanation.surface: Finding fault with someone who talks during a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap is a sharp rebuke, and also a genre of rhythmic speech over music.

clue.text: Contracted, to take delivery of tea paid for

indicators.note: to take delivery of means one word receives another inside it

parts.note: pursed lips are contracted
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a deal for tea that has been paid for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' suggests an agreement, but it means drawn together.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchased means bought, so it was paid for.

clue.text: Stuff that's needed for PC

definitions.meaning: to stuff is to cram or force in
random access memory, an essential part of a personal computer

explanation.surface: Material a personal computer requires.
explanation.walkthrough: PC here is a personal computer, not a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram is to cram things in, and RAM is the working memory a computer needs.

clue.text: After short time, whale comes to island

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the other

parts.note: min is short for minute
an orca is a killer whale

explanation.surface: A whale reaches an island shortly afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Minorca is one of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Court's formality a warning signal

parts.note: starch is stiffness or formality of manner
the amber traffic light warns that red is coming

explanation.surface: A court's stiff procedure acts as a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: AMBER is the middle traffic light in the UK sequence, warning drivers to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The Star Chamber was an English court of law, abolished in 1641, notorious for arbitrary judgements.

clue.text: Wader used beak on gull

parts.note: a bird bit with its beak
a tern is a seabird related to the gull

explanation.surface: A bird pecking at a gull.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a heron-like wading bird.

clue.text: Animal on rope's secured -it receives papal blessing

indicators.note: secured means the animal holds the other pieces safely inside it

parts.note: a cat is an animal
a cord is a thin rope

explanation.surface: A tethered animal is blessed by the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is an agreement between the Vatican and a state, so it carries the Pope's approval.

clue.text: Love to be a help to Santa

definitions.meaning: one of the reindeer that pull Father Christmas's sleigh

explanation.surface: Love helping Father Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love, and one of Santa's reindeer in the poem.

clue.text: Good match made to start burning

definitions.meaning: to ... is to ignite, as wood ...

explanation.surface: A fine match struck so it begins to burn.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a desirable partner, and a fire catches when it starts to burn.

clue.text: What's primarily carried on ship?

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of the word

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship

explanation.surface: Asking what a ship chiefly transports.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of 'carried', C, plus ARGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the goods a ship carries.

clue.text: Leave a coat

parts.note: to park a car is to leave it somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof coat.

clue.text: Not being nasty to one sticking nose in

definitions.text: Not being nasty to one sticking nose in

parts.words: Not being nasty to one sticking nose in
parts.note: the nose is literal: something that gives off no unpleasant smell to whoever sniffs it

explanation.surface: Staying polite to a meddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticking nose in' suggests a busybody, but the nose is doing the smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no smell at all, so nothing nasty for a sniffer to detect.

clue.text: Dreadfully saddened there can be no progress here

definitions.text: there can be no progress here

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests the letters are wrecked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Feeling miserable because things are going nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead ends are routes or situations that lead nowhere, so no progress is possible.

clue.text: Composer heard with sickly sentiment? No

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: goo is cloying sentimentality, followed by the word no

explanation.surface: A composer listened to with mawkish feeling, then rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: Gounod is said in the French way, goo-noh: GOO plus NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Gounod was a French composer, best known for the opera Faust.
